metaTitle: Aboakyer: the Deer Hunt Festival of Winneba
metaDescription: Aboakyer is the deer hunt festival of the Effutu of Winneba, held in early May: two Asafo companies race to catch a live bushbuck for the god Penkye Otu. Story, days and tips.
subtitle: Winneba’s race to catch a live bushbuck
answer: Aboakyer is the deer hunt festival of the Effutu people of Winneba in the Central Region. On a Saturday at the start of May, two Asafo companies, the Tuafo and the Dentsefo, race into the bush to catch a live bushbuck with sticks, clubs and their hands. The first to bring it to the paramount chief wins, and the animal is offered to the god Penkye Otu.

sticky.title: Early May
sticky.text: Be in Winneba on the Saturday morning: the hunters set out at dawn.

schema.description: Deer hunt festival of the Effutu of Winneba, in which two Asafo companies race to catch a live bushbuck.

sections.title: The story behind the hunt
sections.html:
Aboakyer remembers the migration of the Effutu, the Simpa people, south to Winneba, and grew from sacrifices to their god Otu for a good harvest and protection from evil.[[1]]

By tradition the priest first demanded a young member of the royal family each year. The people appealed and were allowed a wild cat instead, caught alive, but so many hunters died trying that they appealed again, and Penkye Otu, named after the place where they settled, accepted a young deer.[[1]] That is the animal the Asafo companies still hunt.

days.label: The week before
days.title: Clean-up, health walk and the gods on parade
days.html: In 2024 the festival opened a week ahead with clean-up exercises, a health walk and a parade of the gods through Winneba’s main streets.[[2]]

days.label: Saturday dawn
days.title: The hunt
days.html: The Tuafo No. 1 and Dentsefo No. 2 Asafo companies head for their own hunting grounds at dawn, carrying sticks and clubs and singing war songs.[[1]]

days.label: Saturday
days.title: The catch
days.html: The first company to bring a live bushbuck to the Omanhen wins. Coming back empty-handed is a bad omen, so each hopes the other succeeds too. When word of a catch reaches town, the streets erupt.[[1]] In 2024 the Dentsefo brought in the first bushbuck and the Tuafo followed.[[2]]

days.label: Saturday afternoon
days.title: The durbar
days.html: Chiefs and people gather for a durbar. The Omanhen steps on the bushbuck three times, a sign that Penkye Otu accepts it, before the rites continue.[[1,2]]

sections.title: Good to know if you go
tips: Where: Winneba is on the coast road between Accra and Cape Coast, about an hour or two from Accra.
When: the hunt is on the Saturday; the durbar is in the afternoon. Come early to see the companies set off.
Keep clear: the companies move fast and in force when they return with a catch. Watch from the side of the road.
Respect the rites: some rituals are sacred and not for cameras. Ask before photographing chiefs, priests or anyone taking part, and follow what the ushers ask.
Back in January: Winneba also hosts the Winneba Masquerade on New Year’s Day.

faq.a: The deer hunt festival of the Effutu people of Winneba, in which two Asafo companies race to catch a live bushbuck for the god Penkye Otu.
It runs for about a week and peaks on a Saturday at the start of May. In 2024 it opened on 27 April.

faq.q: Who are the Tuafo and Dentsefo?
faq.a: The two Asafo (warrior) companies of Winneba, No. 1 and No. 2, who compete in the hunt.
